newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese unhappy with their bureaucrats - survey.
newsitem.headline: Japanese unhappy with their bureaucrats - survey.

text.p: The Japanese think their public servants are irresponsible in their handling of money and cannot be trusted, according to a newspaper poll released on Thursday.
A poll by the Asahi Shimbun, conducted amid a series of corruption scandals, found that 65 percent of those surveyed said they do not trust government bureaucrats.
Only 32 percent said they do have faith in bureaucrats, down 12 percentage points from a similar survey in May 1994.
Asked about the recent arrest of a former vice health minister, 44 percent said their main concern was that bureaucrats did not know how to handle money.
The former official, Nobuharu Okamitsu, was arrested earlier this month on suspicion of taking 60 million yen ($530,000) in bribes from a business executive.
In addition, 28 percent said there is misuse of taxpayer money, while 21 percent said the scandal shook their faith in the government-run health care system.

When asked what causes scandals by bureaucrats, 51 percent of the participants blamed the existing cozy relationship between politicians and public servants, 27 percent said the bureaucracy enjoys too much power and 15 percent said bureaucrats have low morals.
The survey was conducted over the telephone last Sunday and Monday and asked 2,000 people about political issues currently affecting the nation.
